extracted.intended_audience: novelists, critics, and students of fiction (writers and critical readers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on analysing and producing the modern novel: how to read so as to perceive a book's form and how to choose and apply techniques (point of view, scene, picture, selection, arrangement) when constructing fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: The craft (form and making) as primary object of judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: The finished form of the thing — the novel as made — is the proper object for judgment: 'the whole of the matter is contained within the finished form of the thing, and that the form was fashioned by the craft.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism should watch the novelist 'at his work' and focus on how the book was made rather than on broad metaphysical talk about 'art'. Attend to workmanship, deliberate movement, and the manner of making the book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read aright / reconstructive reading
rubrics_metrics.description: The critic/reader must 'read aright' by holding the world of the novel at a distance and deliberately reconstructing the book's form instead of losing oneself in the novel's illusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid simply dwelling in scenes or characters; practice 'creative reading' to gather impressions into a single image of the book, watching its progress page by page so the critic can judge how it was made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form, design, and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: A novel has a form that can be more or less good: design, proportion, and composition are qualities to seek in fiction (though applied loosely compared with other arts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the novel's shape is coherent and if it functions for the work's purposes; recognize that some novels may succeed despite formal defects, but form remains an important criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization / command of life
rubrics_metrics.description: The author’s command of life — grasp of character and knowledge of human affections and manners — is a central measure of a novelist's achievement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether characters (e.g., Clarissa, Anna, Emma) are powerfully realized and persist in the reader’s mind; consider the novelist’s capacity to create convincing human beings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth, vividness, and convincingness (likeness to life)
rubrics_metrics.description: A novel, as a 'picture of life,' should be true, vivid, and convincing — it should resemble life convincingly enough to be taken as a representation of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the reader's ordinary imaginative faculties plus taste to decide whether the book 'realizes' life well; this is distinct from mere novelty or ornament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate choice and handling of point of view
rubrics_metrics.description: Choosing the point of view is decisive for how a subject is to be approached; the point of view gives the general 'look' of the story and determines which instruments of the craft are proper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide early what consciousness or vantage will govern the book and be consistent; interpose a presence between author and reader when that strengthens the work, and be aware of the ramifications of centring the story in someone's mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: The dramatic scene (dramatic incident) as the highest-value instrument
rubrics_metrics.description: The scene — a dramatized incident where action is shown directly — is of primary importance; it delivers the 'final stroke' and is the sharpest effect available to the novelist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use scenes sparingly and strategically (they are 'expensive' in time/space). Scenes should typically clinch matters or demonstrate results already prepared by other means; avoid wasting or weakening a scene by misplacing it.

rubrics_metrics.name: The pictorial/panoramic method (picture) and its role
rubrics_metrics.description: Picture or panoramic survey (extended descriptive/narrative passages) can cover time and space economically and accumulate impressions over a stretch; it is generally preparatory and subordinate to drama.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ picture where breadth, accumulated impression, or movement across time is needed; do not expect pictorial report alone to have the force of dramatized scenes, but use its strengths in combination with drama.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy and appropriateness of treatment (scene vs. narrative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different means (scene, picture, narrative summary) have distinct properties and costs; the writer must choose which is appropriate at each stage of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid forcing a mode to do what it does poorly (e.g., using dramatization where a concise narrative would suffice). Reserve slow, fully dramatized scenes for moments that justify their cost; use summary or pictorial methods for distance and economy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and arrangement (authorial selection and ordering)
rubrics_metrics.description: Novel-making is an act of selection from life and arranging those selected materials into an embracing design; the novel's power depends on what the author chooses to keep and how he orders it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the novelist’s judgment in selection (what is emphasized or omitted) and the ordering of material to produce a coherent, welded mass; selection is the novelist's primary creative act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid direct authorial telling; dramatize the mind (mediated presentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The novelist often interposes another presence (a character's consciousness or a mediated narrator) between himself and the reader to convert limitations of pictorial report into dramatic advantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer methods that let the reader see the author's mind (or a character's mind) as a visible object; dramatizing consciousness can turn the thinness of mere report into a strong artistic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity and coherence ('welded mass')
rubrics_metrics.description: A successful novel should result in a single, coherent object — a 'welded mass' that represents the author's intention despite the book arriving in the reader's experience as a flow of impressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the disparate parts are held together by design and whether the whole reads as an integral form rather than a loose procession of episodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation, foreshadowing, and structural support for scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Dramatic scenes require prior preparation; a scene lacking adequate preparation is likely wasting strength and failing to achieve full effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure important scenes are foreshadowed or built up by prior material so they can act swiftly and sharply; use other means (picture, narrative) to prepare the scene's context and stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use limitations as artistic resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize inherent weaknesses of particular methods (e.g., the thinness of pictorial report) and deliberately adopt them as a feature to be exploited rather than concealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a method has an intrinsic limitation, make that limitation central to the technique (e.g., making the mind or 'mirror' the object) so it becomes a distinctive strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: The reader as co-creator / critic-as-novelist
rubrics_metrics.description: A critical reader must take responsibility for recreating the author's book in his own mind; the critic is, in a sense, a novelist who must assemble the impressions into a form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics should approach reading as a creative act — actively constructing the book's form — not merely passively consuming its life-like elements; this aids precise judgment of the craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discriminate beyond mere preference
rubrics_metrics.description: Judgement of fiction should not rest on simple likes/dislikes ('I like you, I bless you' vs 'I like you not, I damn you') but on consistent, informed discrimination that survives scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate a steady, unhurried mind and criteria that mark solid praise or blame; avoid collapses into mere personal taste when evaluating craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical knowledge of craft as prerequisite to criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Useful criticism requires familiarity with the technical aspects of novel-making (scene, picture, point of view, selection, arrangement); without this knowledge criticism remains superficial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study how novels are built — the 'technical aspect' — and read constructively; attend to workmanship rather than repeating generalities about an author's gifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate by how the book was made (craft over reputation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical attention should be fixed upon the question 'How was the book made?' rather than relying on reputation, lists of authorial virtues, or biographical generalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base appraisal on concrete inspection of the novel's construction, even knowing perfect precision is impossible; seek to 'overtake the author at his work' and examine the process of making the book.
